source_text:
Ἔδειξέ μοι ἐπὶ συμψελλίου καθημένους ἀνθρώπους καὶ ἕτερον ἄνθρωπον καθήμενον ἐπὶ καθέδραν, καὶ λέγει μοι: Βλέπεις τοὺς ἐπὶ τοῦ συμψελλίου καθημένους; Βλέπω, φημί, κύριε. Οὗτοι, φησί, πιστοί εἰσι, καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τὴν καθέδραν ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν, ὃς ἀπόλλυσι τὴν διάνοιαν τῶν δούλων τοῦ θεοῦ: τῶν διψύχων δὲ ἀπόλλυσιν, οὐ τῶν πιστῶν.
οὗτοι οὖν οἱ δίψυχοι ὡς ἐπὶ μάντιν ἔρχονται καὶ ἐπερωτῶσιν αὐτόν, τί ἄρα ἔσται αὐτοῖς: κἀκεῖνος ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης, μηδεμίαν ἔχων ἐν ἑαυτῷ δύναμιν πνεύματος θείου, λαλεῖ μετ’ αὐτῶν κατὰ τὰ ἐπερωτήματα αὐτῶν καὶ κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῆς πονηρίας αὐτῶν καὶ πληροῖ τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν, καθὼς αὐτοὶ βούλονται.
αὐτὸς γὰρ κενὸς ὢν κενὰ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται κενοῖς: ὃ γὰρ ἐὰν ἐπερωτηθῇ, πρὸς τὸ κένωμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀποκρίνεται. τινὰ δὲ καὶ ῥήματα ἀληθῆ λαλεῖ: ὁ γὰρ διάβολος πληροῖ αὐτὸν τῷ αὐτοῦ πνεύματι, εἴ τινα δυνήσεται ῥῆξαι τῶν δικαίων.
ὅσοι οὖν ἰσχυροί εἰσιν ἐν τῇ πίστει τοῦ κυρίου, ἐνδεδυμένοι τὴν ἀλήθειαν, τοῖς τοιούτοις πνεύμασιν οὐ κολλῶνται, ἀλλ’ ἀπέχονται ἀπ’ αὐτῶν: ὅσοι δὲ δίψυχοί εἰσι καὶ πυκνῶς μετανοοῦσι, μαντεύονται ὡς καὶ τὰ ἔθνη καὶ ἑαυτοῖς μείζονα ἁμαρτίαν ἐπιφέρουσιν εἰδωλολατροῦντες: ὁ γὰρ ἐπερωτῶν ψευδοπροφήτην περὶ πράξεώς τινος εἰδωλολάτρης ἐστὶ καὶ κενὸς ἀπὸ τῆς ἀληθείας καὶ ἄφρων.
πᾶν γὰρ πνεῦμα ἀπὸ θεοῦ δοθὲν οὐκ ἐπερωτᾶται, ἀλλὰ ἔχον τὴν δύναμιν τῆς θεότητος ἀφ̓ ἑαυτοῦ λαλεῖ πάντα, ὅτι ἄνωθέν ἐστιν ἀπὸ τῆς δυνάμεως τοῦ θείου πνεύματος.
τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα τὸ ἐπερωτώμενον καὶ λαλοῦν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπίγειόν ἐστι καὶ ἐλαφρόν, δύναμιν μὴ ἔχον: καὶ ὅλως οὐ λαλεῖ, ἐὰν μὴ ἐπερωτηθῇ.
Πῶς οὖν, φημί, κύριε, ἄνθρωπος γνώσεται, τίς αὐτῶν προφήτης καὶ τίς ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν; Ἄκουε, φησί, περὶ ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν: καὶ ὥς σοι μέλλω λέγειν, οὕτω δοκιμάσεις τὸν προφήτην καὶ τὸν ψευδοπροφήτην. ἀπὸ τῆς ζωῆς δοκίμαζε τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν ἔχοντα τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον.
πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἄνωθεν πραΰς ἐστι καὶ ἡσύχιος και ταπεινόφρων καὶ ἀπεχόμενος ἀπὸ πάσης πονηρίας καὶ ἐπιθυμίας ματαίας τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου καὶ ἑαυτὸν ἐνδεέστερον ποιεῖ πάντων τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνεται ἐπερωτώμενος, οὐδὲ καταμόνας λαλεῖ, οὐδὲ ὅταν θέλῃ ἄνθρωπος λαλεῖν, λαλεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, ἀλλὰ τότε λαλεῖ, ὅταν θελήσῃ αὐτὸν ὁ θεὸς λαλῆσαι.
ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ ἔχων τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων τῶν ἐχόντων πίστιν θείου πνεύματος καὶ ἔντευξις γένηται πρὸς τὸν θεὸν τῆς συναγωγῆς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων, τότε ὁ ἄγγελος τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος ὁ κείμενος πρὸς αὐτὸν πληροῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ πληρωθεὶς ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ λαλεῖ εἰς τὸ πλῆθος, καθὼς ὁ κύριος βούλεται.
οὕτως οὖν φανερὸν ἔσται τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς θεότητος. ὅση οὖν περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τῆς θεότητος τοῦ κυρίου ἡ δύναμις αὕτη.
ἄκουε νῦν, φησί, περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐπιγείου καὶ κενοῦ καὶ δύναμιν μὴ ἔχοντος, ἀλλὰ ὄντος μωροῦ.
πρῶτον μὲν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος ὁ δοκῶν πνεῦμα ἔχειν ὑψοῖ ἑαυτὸν καὶ θέλει πρωτοκαθεδρίαν ἔχειν, καὶ εὐθὺς ἰταμός ἐστι καὶ ἀναιδὴς καὶ πολύλαλος καὶ ἐν τρυφαῖς πολλαῖς ἀναστρεφόμενος καὶ ἐν ἑτέραις πολλαῖς ἀπάταις καὶ μισθοὺς λαμβάνων τῆς προφητείας αὐτοῦ: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ λάβῃ, οὐ προφητεύει. δύναται οὖν πνεῦμα θεῖον μισθοὺς λαμβάνειν καὶ προφητεύειν; οὐκ ἐνδέχεται τοῦτο ποιεῖν θεοῦ προφήτην, ἀλλὰ τῶν τοιούτων προφητῶν ἐπίγειόν ἐστι τὸ πνεῦμα.
εἶτα ὅλως εἰς συναγωγὴν ἀνδρῶν δικαίων οὐκ ἐγγίζει, ἀλλ’ ἀποφεύγει αὐτούς: κολλᾶται δὲ τοῖς διψύχοις καὶ κενοῖς καὶ κατὰ γωνίαν αὐτοῖς προφητεύει καὶ ἀπατᾷ αὐτοὺς λαλῶν κατὰ τὰς ἐπιθυμίας αὐτῶν πάντα κενῶς: κενοῖς γὰρ καὶ ἀποκρίνεται: τὸ γὰρ κενὸν σκεῦος μετὰ τῶν κενῶν συντιθέμενον οὐ θραύεται, ἀλλὰ συμφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις.
ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ εἰς συναγωγὴν πλήρη ἀνδρῶν δικαίων ἐχόντων πνεῦμα θεότητος καὶ ἔντευξις ἀπ’ αὐτῶν γένηται, κενοῦται ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος, καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἐπίγειον ἀπὸ τοῦ φόβου φεύγει ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ κωφοῦται ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖνος καὶ ὅλως συνθραύεται, μηδὲν δυνάμενος λαλῆσαι.
ἐὰν γὰρ εἰς ἀποθήκην στιβάσῃς οἶνον ἢ ἔλαιον καὶ ἐν αὐτοῖς θῇς κεράμιον κενόν, καὶ πάλιν ἀποστιβάσαι θελήσῃς τὴν ἀποθήκην, τὸ κεράμιον ἐκεῖνο, ὃ ἔθηκας κενόν, κενὸν καὶ εὑρήσεις: οὕτω καὶ οἱ προφῆται οἱ κενοὶ ὅταν ἔλθωσιν εἰς πνεύματα δικαίων, ὁποῖοι ἦλθον, τοιοῦτοι καὶ εὑρίσκονται.
ἔχεις ἀμφοτέρων τῶν προφητῶν τὴν ζωήν. δοκίμαζε οὖν ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων καὶ τῆς ζωῆς τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν λέγοντα ἑαυτὸν πνευματοφόρον εἶναι.
σὺ δὲ πίστευε τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἐρχομένῳ ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἔχοντι δύναμιν: τῷ δὲ πνεύματι τῷ ἐπιγείῳ καὶ κενῷ μηδὲν πίστευε, ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ δύναμις οὐκ ἔστιν: ἀπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου γὰρ ἔρχεται.
ἄκουσον οὖν τὴν παραβολήν, ἣν μέλλω σοι λέγειν: λάβε λίθον καὶ βάλε εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, ἴδε, εἰ δύνασαι ἅψασθαι αὐτοῦ: ἢ πάλιν λάβε σίφωνα ὕδατος καὶ σιφώνισον εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, ἴδε, εἰ δύνασαι τρυπῆσαι τὸν οὐρανόν.
Πῶς, φημί, κύριε, δύναται ταῦτα γενέσθαι; ἀδύνατα γὰρ ἀμφότερα ταῦτα εἴρηκας. Ὡς ταῦτα οὖν, φησίν, ἀδύνατά ἐστιν, οὕτω καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἐπίγεια ἀδύνατά ἐστι καὶ ἀδρανῆ.
λάβε οὖν τὴν δύναμιν τὴν ἄνωθεν ἐρχομένην: ἡ χάλαζα ἐλάχιστόν ἐστι κοκκάριον, καὶ ὅταν ἐπιπέσῃ ἐπὶ κεφαλὴν ἀνθρώπου, πῶς πόνον παρέχει; ἢ πάλιν λάβε σταγόνα, ἣ ἀπὸ τοῦ κεράμου πίπτει χαμαὶ καὶ τρυπᾷ τὸν λίθον.
βλέπεις οὖν, ὅτι τὰ ἄνωθεν ἐλάχιστα πίπτοντα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν μεγάλην δύναμιν ἔχει: οὕτω καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ θεῖον ἄνωθεν ἐρχόμενον δυνατόν ἐστι: τούτῳ οὖν τῷ πνεύματι πίστευε, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ ἑτέρου ἀπέχου.
orientation: The Shepherd gives Hermas the eleventh commandment and shows him a scene: believers on a bench and a false prophet on a chair. Hermas learns to test a prophet by the life he leads.
pass_a_gloss: He showed me upon a bench sitting men and another man sitting upon a chair, and he says to me: Do you see the [ones] upon the bench sitting? I see, I say, lord. These, he says, faithful are, and the [one] sitting upon the chair a false prophet is, who destroys the mind of the servants of God: of the double-minded [ones] however he destroys, not of the faithful [ones]. These therefore the double-minded [ones] as to a diviner come and ask him, what then will be to them: and that [one] the false prophet, no having in himself power of divine spirit, speaks with them according to the questions of them and according to the desires of the wickedness of them and fills the souls of them, just as they themselves wish. He himself for empty being empty [things] also answers to empty [ones]: what for if he is asked, toward the emptiness of the man he answers. Some however also words true he speaks: the for devil fills him with his spirit, if any he will be able to break of the righteous [ones]. As many therefore strong are in the faith of the Lord, having clothed themselves [with] the truth, to such spirits not cleave, but they keep away from them: as many however double-minded are and frequently repent, they divine as also the nations and to themselves greater sin they bring upon [themselves] idol-worshipping: the for [one] asking a false prophet about a matter some an idolater is and empty from the truth and foolish. Every for spirit from God given not is asked, but having the power of the divinity from itself speaks all [things], because from above it is from the power of the divine spirit. The however spirit the [one] being asked and speaking according to the desires of men earthly is and light, power not having: and wholly not it speaks, if not it is asked. How therefore, I say, lord, a man will know, which of them a prophet and which a false prophet is? Hear, he says, about both of the prophets: and as to you I am about to say, so you will test the prophet and the false prophet. From the life test the man the [one] having the spirit the divine. First indeed the [one] having the spirit the [one] from above gentle is and quiet and humble-minded and keeping away from all wickedness and desire vain of this age and himself needier makes than all men and to no one nothing he answers being asked, nor alone does he speak, nor when a man wishes to speak, speaks the spirit the holy, but then he speaks, when God wishes him to speak. When therefore comes the man the [one] having the spirit the divine into a gathering of men righteous of the [ones] having faith of divine spirit and intercession happens toward God of the gathering of those men, then the angel of the prophetic spirit the [one] lying upon him fills the man, and filled the man with the spirit the holy speaks to the multitude, just as the Lord wishes. Thus therefore manifest will be the spirit of the divinity. So great therefore about the spirit of the divinity of the Lord the power [is] this. Hear now, he says, about the spirit the earthly and empty and power not having, but being foolish. First indeed that man the [one] seeming spirit to have exalts himself and wishes first seat to have, and immediately bold he is and shameless and talkative and in luxuries many living and in other many deceits and wages taking of his prophecy: if however he does not take, he does not prophesy. Can therefore a divine spirit wages take and prophesy? Not is it possible this to do a prophet of God, but of such prophets earthly is the spirit. Then wholly to a gathering of righteous men not he draws near, but he flees them: he cleaves however to the double-minded and empty [ones] and in a corner to them he prophesies and deceives them speaking according to the desires of them all [things] emptily: to empty [ones] for also he answers: the for empty vessel with the empty [ones] put together not is broken, but they agree with one another. When however he comes into a gathering full of righteous men having spirit of divinity and intercession from them happens, emptied is that man, and the spirit the earthly from the fear flees from him, and made dumb is that man and wholly is shattered, nothing being able to speak. If for into a storehouse you store wine or oil and among them you place a jar empty, and again to unstore you wish the storehouse, that jar, which you placed empty, empty also you will find: so also the prophets the empty [ones] when they come into spirits of righteous [men], such as they came, such also they are found. You have of both of the prophets the life. Test therefore from the works and the life the man the [one] saying himself spirit-bearer to be. You however believe the spirit the [one] coming from God and having power: the however spirit the earthly and empty in nothing believe, because in it power not is: from the devil for it comes. Hear therefore the parable, which I am about to say to you: take a stone and throw into the heaven, see, if you can touch it: or again take a siphon of water and squirt into the heaven, see, if you can pierce the heaven. How, I say, lord, can these [things] happen? Impossible for both these [things] you have said. As these [things] therefore, he says, impossible are, so also the spirits the earthly impossible are and powerless. Take therefore the power the [one] from above coming: the hail smallest is a grain, and when it falls upon head of a man, how pain does it cause? Or again take a drop, which from the roof falls to the ground and pierces the stone. You see therefore, that the [things] from above smallest falling upon the earth great power have: so also the spirit the divine from above coming powerful is: this therefore spirit believe, from however the other keep away.

choices.why: A simple piece of seating furniture, distinct from the chair (καθέδρα) of the false prophet; 'bench' keeps the contrast plain.
The standard English term for one who falsely claims to speak for God; the passage is entirely about distinguishing true from false prophecy.
The double-minded come to the false prophet 'as to a diviner', a pagan practice; 'diviner' preserves the pagan connotation.
The false prophet answers 'toward the emptiness of the man'; 'emptiness' keeps the abstract noun parallel with the empty vessel imagery.
The false prophet wants the place of honor; 'first seat' is literal and clear.
The man claims to be a 'spirit-bearer'; the compound is kept to show the claim of carrying the Spirit.

pass_b_english: The Shepherd showed me some people sitting on a bench, and another man sitting on a chair. He said to me, “Do you see the people sitting on the bench?” “I see them, sir,” I said. “They are faithful,” he said, “and the man sitting on the chair is a false prophet, who destroys the mind of the servants of God. But it is the mind of the double-minded that he destroys, not the mind of the faithful.

“So these double-minded people come to him as they would to a soothsayer, and they ask him what is going to happen to them. And that false prophet has no power of a divine Spirit in him. He speaks with them according to their questions and according to their wicked desires, and he fills their souls just as they themselves wish.

“For he is empty himself, and he gives empty answers to empty people. Whatever he is asked, he answers to match the emptiness of the person. Yet he does speak some true words. For the devil fills him with his own spirit, to see whether he can break any of the righteous.

“So all who are strong in the faith of the Lord, who have put on the truth, do not cling to such spirits. They keep away from them. But all who are double-minded, who are forever repenting, turn to soothsaying, just as the nations do, and they bring a greater sin upon themselves by their idolatry. For anyone who consults a false prophet about any matter is an idolater, empty of the truth, and senseless.

“For no spirit given by God is consulted. It has the power of divinity and speaks everything of its own accord, because it is from above, from the power of the divine Spirit. But the spirit that is consulted, and that speaks according to people’s desires, is earthly and fickle, and has no power. It does not speak at all unless it is consulted.”

“How then, sir,” I said, “will a person know which of them is a prophet and which is a false prophet?” “Hear,” he said, “about both kinds of prophet. As I am about to tell you, so you shall test the prophet and the false prophet. Test the man who has the divine Spirit by his life.

“First, the one who has the Spirit from above is gentle and quiet and humble. He keeps away from all wickedness and from the empty desire of this age. He makes himself needier than everyone else. He gives no answer to anyone when he is consulted, and he does not speak in private. The Holy Spirit does not speak when a man wants to speak. He speaks at the time when God wants him to speak.

“So the man who has the divine Spirit comes into a gathering of righteous men who have faith in the divine Spirit, and that gathering makes its prayer to God. Then the angel of the prophetic Spirit who is assigned to him fills the man. And the man, filled with the Holy Spirit, speaks to the multitude as the Lord wills.
“In this way, then, the Spirit of divinity will be made plain. Such, then, is the power of the Spirit of the Lord’s divinity.

“Now hear,” he said, “about the spirit that is earthly and empty, that has no power but is foolish. First, the man who seems to have a spirit exalts himself and wants to have the chief seat. At once he is brash and shameless and full of talk. He lives among many luxuries and many other deceits, and he takes pay for his prophecy. If he is not paid, he does not prophesy. Can a divine Spirit take pay and prophesy? It is not possible for a prophet of God to do this. No, the spirit of such prophets is earthly.

“Next, he never comes near a gathering of righteous men. He shuns them. He clings to the double-minded and the empty, and prophesies to them in a corner. He deceives them, saying everything emptily, to suit their desires. For it is empty people he is answering. For an empty vessel set among other empty vessels is not broken. They agree with one another.

“But when he comes into a gathering full of righteous men who have the Spirit of divinity, and they make their prayer, that man is emptied. The earthly spirit flees from him in fear. The man is struck dumb and is altogether shattered, unable to say anything.

“For suppose you stack wine or oil in a storeroom and set an empty jar among them, and later you want to clear the storeroom out. You will find that jar empty, just as you set it there. So it is with the empty prophets. When they come among the spirits of righteous men, they are found to be just what they were when they came.
“You now have the life of both kinds of prophet. So test by his deeds and his life the man who says that he bears the Spirit.
“As for you, put your faith in the Spirit that comes from God and has power. But put no faith at all in the earthly and empty spirit, because there is no power in it. For it comes from the devil.

“Hear, then, the parable I am about to tell you. Take a stone and throw it at the sky, and see whether you can touch the sky. Or again, take a water squirt and squirt it at the sky, and see whether you can pierce the sky.”
“Sir,” I said, “how can these things be done? Both the things you have named are impossible.” “Just as these things cannot be done,” he said, “so the earthly spirits can do nothing, and are feeble.

“Now take the power that comes from above. A hailstone is a very small grain, yet when it falls on a man’s head, what pain it gives! Or again, take the drop that falls from the roof tile to the ground and bores a hole in the stone.

“You see, then, that the smallest things, falling from above onto the earth, have great power. So also the divine Spirit, coming from above, is powerful. Put your faith in this Spirit, then, and keep away from the other.”

problems.quote: For every spirit given from God is not asked questions, but having the power of divinity it speaks everything from itself
problems.why: 'Power of divinity' is awkward; may mean 'divine power' or 'power of foreknowledge'.

edits.old: For every spirit given from God is not asked questions, but having the power of divinity it speaks everything from itself
edits.new: For every spirit given from God is not asked questions, but having divine power it speaks everything from itself

fixed: Changed 'the power of divinity' to 'divine power' to match the source's 'τὴν δύναμιν τῆς θεότητος' more naturally.

polish.changed: Clarified speaker transitions, resolved ambiguous pronouns, smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud, and clarified the meaning of the Spirit speaking spontaneously rather than on demand.

notes.why: Elect, saints, and 'called' seem to overlap but may not be identical categories; reader cannot tell if these are synonyms or distinct groups.
notes.fix: Note whether 'elect' and 'saints' are being used interchangeably or distinctly.

notes.quote: For every spirit given from God is not asked questions, but having divine power it speaks everything from itself
notes.why: This seems to forbid all questioning of prophets, but the text itself shows Hermas asking questions constantly; likely means the Spirit speaks spontaneously, not on demand.
notes.fix: Clarify: the true prophet does not need to be interrogated but speaks God's word spontaneously.

polish.changed: Clarified the false prophet's deceptive influence as 'swells their souls' rather than 'fills', replaced the anachronistic 'siphon' with 'waterskin', and distinguished 'hailstone' from the greeting 'hail' to remove the confusion in the parable.

notes.why: 'Siphon' is anachronistic and odd; the Greek likely means a waterskin or squirt-bottle.
